definitions.explanation: A staged dramatic work in which much or all of the text is sung, with orchestral accompaniment. Includes both individual works and the genre as a whole.

examples.japanese: ⟦{母|はは}→母：00549_haha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧オペラ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大好|だいす}き→大好き：02911_daisuki⟧だ。
⟦{昨夜|さくや}→昨夜：02999_sakuya⟧、⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧なオペラ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{観|み}→観る：22793_miru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}った→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: Last night I went to see a famous opera.

examples.japanese: ⟦イタリア→イタリア：19423_itaria⟧⟦{語|ご}→〜語：09841_go⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧オペラ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{字幕|じまく}→字幕：04446_jimaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あった→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦{方|ほう}→方：01139_hou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{楽|たの}しめる→楽しむ：01203_tanoshimu⟧。
examples.english: Italian operas are easier to enjoy with subtitles.

notes:
From Italian "opera." The Japanese word covers both individual works and the genre. Often paired with verbs like ⟦{観|み}る→観る：22793_miru⟧ (to watch) or ⟦{聴|き}く→聴く：30010_kiku⟧ (to listen to).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- オペラ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{観|み}る→観る：22793_miru⟧: to see an opera
- オペラ⟦{歌手|かしゅ}→歌手：00197_kashu⟧: opera singer
- オペラ{座|ざ}: opera house (⟦パリ→パリ：25088_pari⟧オペラ{座|ざ}: Paris Opera)
- ⟦{本格|ほんかく}→本格：21636_honkaku⟧オペラ: a full-scale opera production

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ミュージカル: musical — songs alternate with spoken dialogue; lighter style
- ⟦{歌劇|かげき}→歌劇：13234_kageki⟧: literal Japanese translation "sung drama"; mostly used in formal/written contexts and proper names ({宝塚|たからづか}{歌劇団|かげきだん})
